title: "Convergence of the Student's t-Distribution to the Normal Distribution"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"

## Limiting Distribution of the Student T

In this section, we illustrate the limiting behavior of the Student’s t-distribution as the degrees of freedom (𝜈) increase. The Student’s t-distribution is known to approximate the Standard Normal Distribution as 𝜈 \rightarrow \infty, since the variability due to estimating the population variance decreases with larger sample sizes.

The R code below generates several t-distributions with different degrees of freedom — specifically, 𝜈 = 2, 5, 10, 30, 100 ν = 2,5,10,30,100 — and compares them to the standard normal curve N(0,1)

The steps performed in the code are as follows:

Generate x-values from −4 to 4 to represent the range of both distributions.

Compute probability densities for multiple t-distributions using the dt() function and for the normal distribution using dnorm().

Combine all results into a single data frame suitable for plotting with ggplot2.

Overlay the curves using distinct colors and line types to visualize convergence.

The resulting plot demonstrates that as the degrees of freedom increase, the t-distribution’s tails become thinner, and its shape approaches the normal distribution.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required package
library(ggplot2)

# Define a sequence of x-values
x <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 400)

# Define degrees of freedom for multiple t-distributions
dfs <- c(2, 5, 10, 30, 100)

# Create a data frame for plotting
df_data <- data.frame(
  x = rep(x, times = length(dfs) + 1),
  density = c(sapply(dfs, function(df) dt(x, df)), dnorm(x)),
  Distribution = factor(rep(c(paste0("t(df=", dfs, ")"), "Normal(0,1)"), each = length(x)),
                        levels = c(paste0("t(df=", dfs, ")"), "Normal(0,1)"))
)

# Plot the t-distributions and the normal distribution
ggplot(df_data, aes(x = x, y = density, color = Distribution, linetype = Distribution)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#FF6666", "#FF9933", "#66CC66", "#3399FF", "#9966CC", "black")) +
  labs(
    title = "Convergence of the Student's t-Distribution to the Normal Distribution",
    subtitle = "As degrees of freedom increase, the t-distribution approaches N(0,1)",
    x = "x",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#003366"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

```
